title: A/B traffic drift and cache-key collision caused blue variant degradation — incident follow-up & runbook hardening
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During an A/B experiment (20% blue, 80% green) deployed to two regions, we observed a progressive degradation in the blue variant's token throughput and a spike in tail latency leading to user-facing errors for a subset of customers. The automated canary health checks did not trigger an immediate rollback because the anomaly prescriptive thresholds were tuned to aggregated latency and not variant-specific prefix drift. Investigation found a KV-cache key collision between model variants and missing tokenization-namespace separation for recent tokenizer changes; as blue's model variant produced longer prefix keys, cache contention and eviction behavior amplified under a sudden regional traffic shift, causing increased compute and OOM throttles on a subset of hosts. This ticket captures the full follow-up: timeline, root cause, actions, runbook edits, telemetry fixes, and long-lived mitigations to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: ~2 hours of degraded responses for 5% of production traffic in eu-west-1 and us-east-1; no data exfiltration; increased token cost during degradation window. Several enterprise customers reported degraded embeddings accuracy for short queries.
timeline: 2026-02-12T09:45Z - Spike in 99th latency observed for blue in eu-west-1; initial alert routed to oncall.
2026-02-12T10:10Z - Autoscaling added capacity but latency persisted; error rate rose to 0.8% for blue.
2026-02-12T10:28Z - Shadow traffic replay and quickcheck test against blue returned higher memory churn.
2026-02-12T10:42Z - Runbook step to abort rollout was not triggered due to aggregated metric thresholding.
2026-02-12T11:00Z - Traffic split manually reverted to 100% green; blue served 0% by 11:05Z.
2026-02-12T11:30Z - Full data collection and traces captured for postmortem analysis.
root_cause: Variant-specific KV cache key namespace overlap combined with a variant tokenizer change (prefix length increase) caused cross-variant cache collisions and accelerated eviction which increased per-request compute on blue hosts. Canary health contract used aggregate cohort metrics; variant-level signal thresholds were too coarse to detect early divergence.
findings: KV cache keys were generated without model-variant namespacing — collisions between v3a and v3b observed under live traffic.
Recent tokenizer upgrade for v3b increased prefix lengths and changed cache hit distribution, increasing memory churn.
Automatic batching behavior exacerbated memory pressure due to longer sequences being sent to the same GPU groups.
Alerting relied on 95th/99th aggregated latency across all variants and regions; variant-specific regressions were under-weighted.
Shadow traffic harness had been sampling requests at 0.5% — insufficient to surface the cache collision under the specific request distribution.
Canary abort rule was configured to evaluate 5m rolling windows; initial regression manifested as a progressive drift over ~20 minutes and was missed.
actions: Immediate: enforce model-variant namespacing for all KV and prefix cache keys (deploy patch runtime-1.19.1).
Short-term: adjust canary health contract to include variant-level 99th latency and memory churn metrics with lower abort hysteresis for A/B experiments.
Short-term: increase shadow sampling to 3% for experiments touching tokenizer code; add synthetic sequences exercising long-prefix paths.
Medium-term: add tokenizer-compatibility gate in model onboarding that verifies cache behavior under synthetic traffic and replay harness.
Medium-term: add a regression test in CI that instruments KV cache distribution and checks for namespace separation across variants.
Long-term: add automated eviction-awareness telemetry and a 'cache-heat' signal that can be used to dynamically throttle variant traffic before hitting OOM thresholds.
Operational: create a lightweight runbook widget in Console showing variant-level telemetry and a one-click abort that auto-rebalances traffic and rescales resources.
runbook_updates: New step: 'Variant Isolation Check' (pre-rollout) — ensures KV keys include model name + variant and logs sample keys.
New alert: 'Variant 99p Memory Churn' — triggers paging and auto-abort when sustained for >10 minutes.
Modify: Canary abort criteria to evaluate both global and per-variant signals with configurable weight; default for model changes is to favor variant signals.
Add: 'Synthetic long-prefix test' to rollout preflight with a configurable sample size and sequence-length distribution.
telemetry_gaps: No explicit metric for cross-variant cache collision rate or namespace overlap.
Shadow traffic sampling rate too low for tokenizer-related regressions.
Lack of a compact per-variant cost/breakdown card in Console during rollouts.
decision_log: 2026-02-13 - Decided to ship KV namespacing patch immediately to reduce blast radius; approved by runtime leads.
2026-02-14 - Agreed to change default shadow sampling to 3% for tokenizer or model-format changes; PM and infra approved CPU/GPU cost tradeoff.
2026-02-20 - Prioritized runbook UI 'one-click abort' as a medium-term UX improvement in console-2026.03 backlog.
review_feedback: PM (Ravi Kapoor): emphasize customer communication templates and SLA implications in runbook.
Design (Maya Torres): suggest a modal that surfaces variant-specific charts with annotations for the abort flow.
SRE (Noah Williams): include a 'cache-heat' derived signal in Alerting Platform and provide mitigation knobs (reduce batch size / shed variant).
status_notes: Patch for KV namespacing merged and staged to canary cluster (runtime-1.19.1-canary). Telemetry PR for variant memory_churn merged. Work remaining: console abort UI, synthetic test harness, and CI regression. Targeting completion by due_date.
estimated_rollback_risk: Low after KV namespacing; initial rollback decision flow will continue to be manual until 'one-click abort' UI is shipped.
